name: Wheat
notes:
Wheat grain, nutrition from USDA (as raw grain/flour). World yield ~2.1 t/ha; the US gets ~3.2 t/ha (USDA NASS 2019–2023). Most wheat grows on former steppe and prairie, which the Land Use sliders weigh lightly. Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra.

Emissions are Poore & Nemecek's 'Wheat & Rye' value (1.57 kg CO2e/kg). That figure is actually per kg of bread and covers milling, baking, transport and retail. It's treated as roughly per kg of grain here (checked 2026-09-24). When wheat is fed to animals, a separate farm-gate value is used instead (0.95 world, 0.37 US), so animals aren't charged for bakery and retail stages. Pesticides (2,4-D and others, ~1.2 kg/ha) and fertilizer are older estimates without a documented derivation. Rye borrows wheat's pesticide profile.
land_types_note: Mostly steppe and prairie (US Plains, Canada, Russia, Ukraine, Argentina).

name: Corn
notes:
Corn (maize) grain, nutrition from USDA (raw grain). World yield ~5.6 t/ha; the US gets ~10.9 t/ha (Corn Belt). Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra (much lower per kg in the US). FAOSTAT production includes corn grown for animal feed and ethanol.

Emissions for eating corn are 1.13 kg CO2e per kg of grain. That was corrected on 2026-09-24 from 1.7, which was Poore & Nemecek's figure per kg of maize meal, not grain. As animal feed, corn uses a farm-gate value (0.79 world, including land-use change; ~0.2–0.33 US). Pesticides (atrazine, glyphosate, metolachlor, ~2.3 kg/ha) are US data that stands in for the world.

Corn oil borrows corn's per-hectare data.
land_types_note: US Corn Belt prairie dominates, with Brazil and tropical smallholder corn making up the rest.

source.title: Poore & Nemecek (2018) — Reducing food's environmental impacts through producers and consumers (Science)
source.note: Corn (Maize) — emissions_per_kg: 1.7 kg CO2e/kg global weighted average (farm gate; includes fertilizer N2O from high-N corn production, farm energy, and land use change; P&N 2018 Table S5 'Maize' category). CORRECTION 2026-09-24: 1.7 is NOT farm gate and is not from Table S5 (Table S5 of the P&N supplement is meat processing conversions). It is the P&N retail-weight mean for 'Maize (Meal)' — functional unit 1 kg of maize meal for polenta (Supplementary Table S1) — and is cradle-to-retail: per kg meal LUC 0.48 + farm 0.72 + processing 0.08 + transport 0.09 + packaging 0.09 + retail 0.04 + losses 0.21 (OWID food-emissions-supply-chain, source 72). Per kg of maize GRAIN (P&N Data S2 Global Totals, source 270) the ex-waste chain total is ~0.99 and farm gate (LUC + farm) is 0.79; see farm_gate_emissions_per_kg. CORRECTION 2026-09-24: value changed 1.7 -> 1.13. Corn's nutrition is whole dry corn GRAIN (FDC 3.65 kcal/g), and its yield and water are per kg grain, but 1.7 is per kg of maize MEAL (degermed, ~0.66 kg meal per kg grain). Converted to per kg grain: 1.70 x 0.664 = 1.13, where 0.664 = P&N farm-gate per kg grain (LUC 0.315 + farm 0.475 = 0.79, Data S2 Global Totals, source 270) / farm-gate per kg meal (0.48 + 0.72 = 1.19, OWID source 72). Cross-check: Data S2 per-kg-grain chain total excluding losses is 0.99; + ~14% losses (P&N meal loss share) ~1.13. Only corn's own food row uses this field; animal feed uses farm_gate_emissions_per_kg, so feed calculations are unchanged. Confidence 2 because the whole chain is scaled by one ratio (meal processing is not separated).

name: Rice
notes:

name: Rice Starch
notes:
Rice starch (used in vegan cheeses), modelled from rice. About 1.25 kg of milled rice makes 1 kg of starch. Land and crop water are rice × 1.25, and per-hectare farm values are copied from rice. No rice starch label exists, so nutrition uses USDA cornstarch as a stand-in (both near-pure starch).

Rice starch takes almost all of the rice's land by weight, while rice protein (made in the same process) uses a value-based share. So the rice field is counted somewhat more than once across the two. Availability (~410 kt) is derived from a market value estimate (confidence 1).

name: Millet
notes:
Millet grain (mostly pearl millet), nutrition from USDA raw millet. Grown in the semi-arid tropics (India, Niger, Nigeria, Mali, Sudan) at ~1 t/ha (FAOSTAT), one of the lowest-yielding grains, so it needs a lot of land per kg. Water is Mekonnen & Hoekstra (4,478 L/kg, almost all rain).

Weak spots: no millet emissions study was found, so emissions use Poore & Nemecek's 'Wheat & Rye' value (1.57) as a cereal proxy, at confidence 1. Real millet could be higher (very low yields) or lower (little fertilizer). Pesticide and fertilizer are borrowed from sorghum (another low-input dryland cereal; confidence 2), added 2026-10-01 after missing data had been scored as zero.
land_types_note: Grown in the semi-arid tropics: India (Rajasthan), Niger, Nigeria, Mali, Sudan and Burkina Faso, plus northern China.
